headline: Wall Street's best week in more than a year was led by chips, even as Treasury yields ended slightly higher, and Brent snapped a three-week losing streak into Sunday's OPEC+ meeting

paragraphs.equities_rates: The AP reports the S&P 500 closed out its best week in more than a year, rising 5.6% from the previous Friday's close, with the PHLX Semiconductor index up 9.25% in the rebound from last week's AI-led rout. Europe and Japan also finished higher, though by less. Treasury yields did not ease with the rally: the 10-year par yield ended at 4.94%, two basis points above the prior Friday after a mid-week low of 4.85% on 25 November, and the two-year rose six basis points to 4.69%. Equities advancing against slightly firmer borrowing costs leave next Friday's November payrolls, which feed straight into the December rate debate, as the test of whether the rebound holds.
paragraphs.metals_fx: Gold recovered 3.5% over the week and silver 5.2%, with platinum also higher, even though the dollar index ended 0.22% firmer and Treasury yields did not fall. That points to a bounce from last week's liquidation and a broader return of risk appetite rather than a change in the rate outlook, which still caps the metals story. Copper barely moved and aluminium finished lower, so the rebound was concentrated in the precious metals.
paragraphs.oil_gas: January Brent settled at $95.44, up 3.1% on the week, ending a three-week losing streak, while January WTI slipped 0.4% to $83.08 for a fourth weekly loss, so the widening gap between the two is the seaborne Gulf risk being priced. Kpler data cited by MarketWatch puts Hormuz flows at only 31% of prewar levels, and the Jazan refinery attack and an Iranian drone strike in Kuwait added to that premium. Sunday's OPEC+ meeting sets 2027 quotas from capacity assessments the Iran war has made hard to pin down. Gas moved the other way on milder weather after the Thanksgiving storm: January Henry Hub fell 6.9% to $3.491, and January TTF lost 4.2% to €84.58 a megawatt-hour.

basis: Week-on-week = Friday 27 November 2026 close versus Friday 20 November 2026 close. Equities, metals, FX, WTI, Henry Hub and TTF, and the official US Treasury 10-year and 2-year par yields, are from emmi-data live-data market.json generated 2026-11-27T22:32:22+01:00 (Yahoo Finance daily bars; Treasury par curve for the two official yield rows). Week-on-week percentages are that file's 1W field (7-calendar-day lookback), checked against the same file's daily OHLC bars. Brent January 2027 (BRNF27, the BZF27 front month) uses ICE settles in emmi-data curves/brent/: 92.57 on 20 Nov and 95.44 on 27 Nov; the same contract was front month on both Fridays (expiry 30 November 2026, not yet rolled). market.json BZ=F matches those settles and the +3.1% week-on-week figure. A later emmi-data futures/ Yahoo/TradingView file for 27 Nov disagreed with the Friday evening settle on Brent, WTI, Henry Hub and TTF, so those Saturday prints were not used. TTF is the January 2027 contract in market.json (88.30 on 20 Nov, 84.58 on 27 Nov); the EEX curve archive's latest official file is 26 November. The 10-year prior-Friday close of 4.92% is implied by the official series' +2 basis-point 1W change on the 4.94% close of 27 Nov (the file's yields10 chart skips 20 Nov). The mid-week 10-year low of 4.85% is the official 25 November close. The two-year prior-Friday close of 4.63% is implied by the official +6 basis-point 1W change on the 4.69% close of 27 Nov.
